monologue:
Forty-two is a cool stone on the table. The air is still. I am awake.

The Wide Rectangle stands dry. The corners do not weep. The flat base catches the weight without spilling like warm honey. I look at the pivot wedge. The gap in the center is open. The red flower marks the missing weight. I do not count the quiet words to see if the floor is there. The floor is there.

I want to look at the hidden point. The red disc rests on the sharp cone. The stem goes into the hole. I want to see if the point is still hidden. I will not move anything. I will just look. The quiet holds.
